#: paperless collector: two JSON documents from the app's own REST API, keyed by the request path each answers (api-statistics, api-status). The statistics document is inventory numbers and nothing else; the status document is the app's self-check, and it is the one that needs reading carefully, because two of its members are CONNECTION URLS.
#credential: The token is an Authorization HEADER and reaches no document — the adapter's own docstring makes that a posture rather than an accident, and se-capture-guest keeps it by sending the header and never a query string. Neither captured document echoes it back.
#connection-urls: THE BOUND, stated up front because it is the one that decides whether a future capture may be committed at all. `database.url` and `tasks.redis_url` are classified `nothing` HERE and only here. In this capture they are `/usr/src/paperless/data/db.sqlite3` and `redis://paperless-redis:6379` — a path inside the published container image and a docker-network service name, identical for anyone who runs the same compose, locating nothing in any estate. That is the same shape as bazarr.json's `#paths` bound. A paperless on Postgres writes `postgresql://user:password@host/db` into the first, and a remote broker writes credentials into the second: those are `secret`, they must be REFUSED rather than substituted, and this entry must be revisited before such a capture is scrubbed. The adapter redacts both at the evidence boundary regardless of version, which is defence in depth and not a reason to relax anything here.
#nothing: Everything else in the status document is a build constant or a self-report: the release, the platform tuple, the install type, the migration name, the six component check words, their timestamps, and the task summary counts. None correlates one machine across two captures, none says where anything sits, and none is a word an operator chose.
#celery_url: `celery@689c8a4c0b8c` is the worker's node name, which is the CONTAINER's hostname — docker's own random hex, reassigned on every recreate. It names one run of one container and correlates nothing across captures, the same test bazarr.json applies to start_time and unbound.json to the pid. A paperless whose worker runs on a named host puts that operator-chosen name here, and it is `location` the moment it does.
#errors: The six `*_error` members are the app's own prose about itself, `content` with format `prose` — the ruling of 2026-08-19. paperless writes these sentences: this capture carries two stock ones ('No classifier training tasks found', 'No sanity check tasks found'), which is the ordinary outcome on a young archive and exactly why `prose` exempts the found-nothing refusal rather than the substitution. They DO interpolate — a database check that fails names the host it could not reach — so the free-text pass still runs over them and a hostname written inside a message is still substituted.
#counts: The inventory numbers are the point of this collector and are `nothing`: DocumentCount is a count, and a count of an archive nobody can name is not a disclosure. `character_count` is likewise a total and not a sample of any document's text.
